purpose: W3C-01 measured that 182 of 3589 tests obtained their authority from the development-preview bypass, and recorded that as a coverage limitation. This entry establishes HOW MANY of them actually prove less than they appear to, rather than leaving the number sounding like 182.

correction_to_W3C-01.what_I_wrote: 'any authorization property they appear to prove should be treated as unproven until re-authored' and 'arguably the more important half of this finding'
correction_to_W3C-01.why_that_was_wrong: It conflated two different things. A test that obtains its authority from a bypass cannot prove a POSITIVE authority claim - 'this role MAY do X' - because the actor held ['*'] rather than that role. But a REFUSAL proven the same way is STRONGER, not weaker: the preview superuser is a strict superset of any named role, so anything refused for it is refused for a lesser actor too. Most of the 182 are refusals or business-logic assertions.
correction_to_W3C-01.the_repository_already_knew: tests/founder-role-escalation.test.mjs states the superset argument explicitly in a comment. tests/provider-availability-write-ownership.test.mjs, tests/route-authorization-class.test.mjs and tests/scheduling-rules-authorization.test.mjs each carry a case asserting that the preview bypass is HOST-GATED, precisely so their own authorization cases are non-vacuous - and those suites use real hosts for every authority claim. The discipline was already there; W3C-01 did not credit it.
correction_to_W3C-01.corrected_severity: The test-suite consequence is NOT the more important half of W3C-01. The production defect - two of three preview branches carrying no environment guard - is.

triage.population: 182 failing test instances / 180 distinct titles, captured by running the suite with NODE_ENV unset after the W3C-01 fix
triage.method: Classified by whether the test's CLAIM is that a named role was PERMITTED something, then every candidate examined by hand. A cross-check swept all 382 suites for tests naming a role and asserting a 2xx on a preview host: 20 matched, and all but one resolved to either a real host (provider-availability uses https://ops.pawspace.example) or a calculation assertion (money-hardening's authorization cases both use callAs with real identities and assert 403).

the_one_genuine_case.test: tests/content-controls.test.mjs - 'real execution: the public GET needs no identity; admin view and mutations are permission-gated'
the_one_genuine_case.what_was_wrong: the ADMIN VIEW half called call(), which drives http://localhost and therefore read as the preview superuser. 'The preview superuser could read the admin view' says nothing about whether an ADMIN may. The gating half was always sound - it uses callAs() with a real customer identity and asserts 403.
the_one_genuine_case.fix: a real app_users row with role_code 'admin' is seeded and the positive half now presents it through callAs()
the_one_genuine_case.sabotage: downgrading that seeded role to 'customer' turns the case RED, which it could not do before

not_claimed: This triages the tests that FAILED without preview - the ones that depended on it to be admitted. A test that passes either way was not relying on the bypass and is out of scope.
The classification of the 111 scaffolding and 24 journey tests is by their assertions, sampled and cross-checked, not exhaustively re-read one by one.
